engineeringSkip.reason: Cryptographically hashing and signing biological memories via an external ledger has no basis in known neuroscience or cryptography — there is no mechanism by which a memory could be hashed, stored or verified, making this a speculative buzzword mash-up rather than an engineering pathway.

factCheck.reason: Memories are not stored as discrete files or codes that can be hashed and signed — they are distributed, constantly re-formed patterns of synaptic strength across the brain, so there is no scientific basis for cryptographic verification or rollback of a biological memory.
